therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of autoreactive T-cell activation and downstream autoimmune inflammation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with active systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) experiencing disease flares
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Number of participants experiencing a new SLE flare from start of corticosteroid taper to Day 365

results.effect_size: Abatacept: 94 participants with new SLE flare (95% CI: 72.4–86.9%); Placebo: 47 participants (95% CI: 72.6–92.3%); HR=1.1 (95% CI: 0.7–1.5)
results.target_engagement_evidence: 2 participants developed antibodies specific for CTLA4-T and abatacept during double-blind period; 30 participants in open-label period
biomarker_changes: Antibodies specific for CTLA4-T and abatacept detected in 2 participants (DB period)
Antibodies specific for CTLA4-T and abatacept detected in 30 participants (OL period)
subgroup_findings: Median days to first SLE flare: 107 days (abatacept) vs 92 days (placebo); HR=1.1 (95% CI: 0.7–1.5)
No difference in SLICC/ACR Damage Index change at 1 year between arms
Open-label period terminated early by Data Monitoring Committee due to failure to meet primary endpoint and increase in SAEs in abatacept group
safety_signals: Higher rate of SAEs in abatacept arm (24/121) vs placebo (4/59) during double-blind period
Higher rate of infections in abatacept arm (71/121) vs placebo (38/59)
Higher rate of peri-infusional AEs in abatacept arm (27/121) vs placebo (13/59)
Open-label period terminated due to increase in SAEs in abatacept group

Serious AEs included pericarditis (2 abatacept), lupus vasculitis (1 placebo), depression (1 abatacept), psychotic disorder (1 abatacept, 1 placebo), hypersensitivity (1 abatacept), drug hypersensitivity (1 abatacept), polyneuropathy (1 abatacept), acute polyneuropathy (1 abatacept), haematemesis (1 abatacept), headache (1 placebo)

context.duration: 12 months double-blind period; open-label period terminated early
context.investigator_commentary: Based on the recommendation of the Data Monitoring Committee, the open-label period was terminated by the sponsor, as the trial failed to meet the primary outcome measure for the double-blind period and because of an increase in SAEs in the abatacept treatment group.

Adults with active SLE experiencing disease flares, treated with abatacept plus prednisone taper
Adults with active SLE experiencing disease flares, treated with placebo plus prednisone taper

results_by_chain.biology_description: suppression of autoreactive T-cell activation and downstream autoimmune inflammation
results_by_chain.population_description: Adults with active SLE who completed the double-blind period and entered the open-label extension

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Prednisone's broad immunosuppression was intended to synergize with abatacept's T-cell co-stimulation blockade to reduce SLE flare rates during steroid taper, but the combination failed to demonstrate superiority over prednisone alone.
modulation_entries.citation: Based on the recommendation of the Data Monitoring Committee, the open-label period was terminated by the sponsor, as the trial failed to meet the primary outcome measure for the double-blind period and because of an increase in SAEs in the abatacept treatment group.
